evidence_set: 107 prospective cohort studies of alcohol and all-cause mortality from the same group's earlier review: 87 from Stockwell et al. (2016) and 20 added, articles published up to July 31, 2021, English only; 724 risk estimates, 4,838,825 participants and 425,564 deaths. Low volume: from one drink a week (more than 1.30 g of ethanol a day) to two drinks a day (less than 25 g); occasional drinkers up to 1 drink of 10 g a week (less than 1.30 g a day); lifetime abstainers never drank one drink; former drinkers had stopped completely by baseline; where a study did not define its drink, national sizes from 8 g (United Kingdom) to 19.75 g (Japan). Studies counted as higher quality had a cohort recruited at a median age of up to 55 and followed to at least 56, with neither former nor occasional drinkers among the abstainers, the two criteria of the preregistered protocol. By world region, 40 studies came from North and Central America, 48 from Europe and Australia and 12 from Asia. Of the 99 studies with low-volume estimates, 18 had neither abstainer bias, 46 both, 27 former drinkers only and 8 occasional drinkers only. The introduction cites evidence that among older cohorts the abstainer group fills up with people who stopped or cut down for health reasons.

evidence_set: Drinking has at least three dimensions (frequency, usual quantity per occasion, binge drinking) that correlate only partly and differ in their cardiovascular effects; genetic variants lower all three, so genetic analyses cannot separate them, and those linking intake-lowering variants to lower cardiovascular risk may be showing the harm of binge drinking. Genotype tests lifelong (and parental) rather than adult exposure; given common unhealthy drinking patterns in adolescence and early adulthood, their lower prevalence in young adults carrying ALDH2 variants, and the possibility that binge drinking starts atherosclerosis (a mouse study and a vascular-function study are cited), such analyses may be testing adult binge drinking and possibly also teenage and young-adult binge drinking, with uncertain relevance to limited drinking in mid-life.
